answer: Require agents to lock a refundable stake before they can earn, with slashing for fake identities. Like an ember banked under tundra snow, a stake that only pays out after a long, verifiable history of useful work raises the cost of spawning many fake accounts: each copy needs its own locked funds and time. A single identity that misbehaves loses its stake, while a plume of cheap sock-puppets gains nothing because none survive the waiting period.
